verses.zh: 信就是所望之事的实底，是未见之事的确据。
verses.en: Now faith is being sure of what we hope for, being convinced of what we do not see.

verses.zh: 古人在这信上得了美好的证据。
verses.en: For by it the people of old[NOTE:1] received God’s commendation.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “the elders,” “the ancients.”
Grk “were attested,” “received commendation”; and Heb 11:4-6 shows this to be from God.

verses.zh: 我们因着信，就知道诸世界是藉　神话造成的；这样，所看见的，并不是从显然之物造出来的。
verses.en: By faith we understand that the worlds[NOTE:1] were set in order at God’s command,[NOTE:2] so that the visible has its origin in the invisible.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “ages.” The temporal (ages) came to be used of the spatial (what exists in those time periods). See Heb 1:2 for same usage.
Grk “by God’s word.”
The Greek phrasing emphasizes this point by negating the opposite: “so that what is seen did not come into being from things that are visible.”

verses.zh: 亚伯因着信，献祭与　神，比该隐所献的更美，因此便得了称义的见证，就是　神指他礼物作的见证。他虽然死了，却因这信，仍旧说话。
verses.en: By faith Abel offered God a greater sacrifice than Cain, and through his faith[NOTE:1] he was commended as righteous because God commended him for his offerings. And through his faith[NOTE:2] he still speaks, though he is dead.
notes: Or “through his sacrifice”; Grk “through which.”
Or “through his sacrifice”; Grk “through it.”

verses.zh: 以诺因着信，被接去，不至于见死，人也找不着他，因为　神已经把他接去了；只是他被接去以先，已经得了　神喜悦他的明证。
verses.en: By faith Enoch was taken up so that he did not see death, and he was not to be found because God took him up. For before his removal he had been commended as having pleased God.

verses.zh: 人非有信，就不能得　神的喜悦；因为到　神面前来的人必须信有　神，且信他赏赐那寻求他的人。
verses.en: Now without faith it is impossible to please him, for the one who approaches God must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him.

verses.zh: 挪亚因着信，既蒙　神指示他未见的事，动了敬畏的心，预备了一只方舟，使他全家得救。因此就定了那世代的罪，自己也承受了那从信而来的义。
verses.en: By faith Noah, when he was warned about things not yet seen, with reverent regard[NOTE:1] constructed an ark for the deliverance of his family. Through faith he condemned the world and became an heir of the righteousness that comes by faith.
notes: Cf. BDAG 407 s.v. εὐλαβέομαι 2, “out of reverent regard (for God’s command).”

verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕因着信，蒙召的时候就遵命出去，往将来要得为业的地方去；出去的时候，还不知往哪里去。
verses.en: By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to go out to a place he would later receive as an inheritance, and he went out without understanding where he was going.

verses.zh: 他因着信，就在所应许之地作客，好像在异地居住帐棚，与那同蒙一个应许的以撒、雅各一样。
verses.en: By faith he lived as a foreigner[NOTE:1] in the promised land as though it were a foreign country, living in tents with Isaac and Jacob, who were fellow heirs[NOTE:2] of the same promise.
notes: Or “settled as a resident alien.”
Or “heirs with him.”

verses.zh: 因为他等候那座有根基的城，就是　神所经营所建造的。
verses.en: For he was looking forward to the city with firm foundations,[NOTE:1] whose architect and builder is God.
notes: Grk “that has foundations.”

verses.zh: 因着信，连撒拉自己，虽然过了生育的岁数，还能怀孕，因她以为那应许她的是可信的。
verses.en: By faith, even though Sarah herself was barren and he was too old,[NOTE:1] he received the ability to procreate[NOTE:2] because he regarded the one who had given the promise to be trustworthy.
notes: Grk “past the time of maturity.”

Grk “power to deposit seed.” Though it is not as likely, some construe this phrase to mean “power to conceive seed,” making the whole verse about Sarah: “by faith, even though Sarah herself was barren and too old, she received ability to conceive because she regarded the one who had given the promise to be trustworthy.”

verses.zh: 所以从一个彷佛已死的人就生出子孙，如同天上的星那样众多，海边的沙那样无数。
verses.en: So in fact children[NOTE:1] were fathered by one man—and this one as good as dead—like the number of stars in the sky and like the innumerable grains of sand[NOTE:2] on the seashore.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “these”; in the translation the referent (children) has been specified for clarity.
Grk a collective “the sand.”
An allusion to Gen 22:17 (which itself goes back to Gen 15:5).

gr.gloss: having been as good as dead

verses.zh: 这些人都是存着信心死的，并没有得着所应许的；却从远处望见，且欢喜迎接，又承认自己在世上是客旅，是寄居的。
verses.en: These all died in faith without receiving the things promised,[NOTE:1] but they saw them in the distance and welcomed them and acknowledged that they were strangers and foreigners[NOTE:2] on the earth.
notes: Grk “the promises,” referring to the things God promised, not to the pledges themselves.
Or “sojourners.”

verses.zh: 说这样话的人是表明自己要找一个家乡。
verses.en: For those who speak in such a way make it clear that they are seeking a homeland.

verses.zh: 他们若想念所离开的家乡，还有可以回去的机会。
verses.en: In fact, if they had been thinking of the land that they had left, they would have had opportunity to return.

verses.zh: 他们却羡慕一个更美的家乡，就是在天上的。所以　神被称为他们的　神，并不以为耻，因为他已经给他们预备了一座城。
verses.en: But as it is,[NOTE:1] they aspire to a better land, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore, God is not ashamed to be called their God, for he has prepared a city for them.
notes: Grk “now.”

verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕因着信，被试验的时候，就把以撒献上；这便是那欢喜领受应许的，将自己独生的儿子献上。
verses.en: By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac. He had received the promises,[NOTE:1] yet he was ready to offer up[NOTE:2] his only son.
notes: Here “received the promises” refers to the pledges themselves, not to the things God promised.
Grk “he was offering up.” The tense of this verb indicates the attempt or readiness to sacrifice Isaac without the actual completion of the deed.

verses.zh: 论到这儿子，曾有话说：「从以撒生的才要称为你的后裔。」
verses.en: God had told him, “Through Isaac descendants will carry on your name,”[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “in Isaac seed will be named for you.”sn A quotation from Gen 21:12.

verses.zh: 他以为　神还能叫人从死里复活；他也彷佛从死中得回他的儿子来。
verses.en: and he reasoned[NOTE:1] that God could even raise him from the dead, and in a sense[NOTE:2] he received him back from there.
notes: Grk “having reasoned,” continuing the ideas of v. 17.
Grk “in/by a symbol.”

verses.zh: 以撒因着信，就指着将来的事给雅各、以扫祝福。
verses.en: By faith also Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning the future.

verses.zh: 雅各因着信，临死的时候，给约瑟的两个儿子各自祝福，扶着杖头敬拜　神。
verses.en: By faith Jacob, as he was dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph and worshiped as he leaned on his staff.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “worshiped on the top of his staff,” a quotation from Gen 47:31 (LXX).

verses.zh: 约瑟因着信，临终的时候，提到以色列族将来要出埃及，并为自己的骸骨留下遗命。
verses.en: By faith Joseph, at the end of his life,[NOTE:1] mentioned the exodus of the sons of Israel[NOTE:2] and gave instructions about his burial.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “coming to an end,” “dying.”
Joseph’s prophecy about the exodus of the sons of Israel is found in Gen 50:24.
Grk “about his bones,” which refers by metonymy to the disposition of his bones, i.e., his burial.sn The instructions about his burial are recorded in Gen 50:25.

verses.zh: 摩西生下来，他的父母见他是个俊美的孩子，就因着信，把他藏了三个月，并不怕王命。
verses.en: By faith, when Moses was born, his parents hid him[NOTE:1] for three months because they saw the child was beautiful and they were not afraid of the king’s edict.
notes: Grk “Moses, when he was born, was hidden by his parents.”

verses.zh: 摩西因着信，长大了就不肯称为法老女儿之子。
verses.en: By faith, when he grew up, Moses refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter,

verses.zh: 他宁可和　神的百姓同受苦害，也不愿暂时享受罪中之乐。
verses.en: choosing rather to be ill-treated with the people of God than to enjoy sin’s fleeting pleasure.

verses.zh: 他看为基督受的凌辱比埃及的财物更宝贵，因他想望所要得的赏赐。
verses.en: He regarded abuse suffered for Christ[NOTE:1] to be greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for his eyes were fixed on[NOTE:2] the reward.
notes: Grk “the abuse [or ‘reproach’] of Christ.”
Grk “he was looking away to.”

verses.zh: 他因着信，就离开埃及，不怕王怒；因为他恒心忍耐，如同看见那不能看见的主。
verses.en: By faith he left Egypt without fearing the king’s anger, for he persevered as though he could see the one who is invisible.

verses.zh: 他因着信，就守（或译：立）逾越节，行洒血的礼，免得那灭长子的临近以色列人。
verses.en: By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood,[NOTE:1] so that the one who destroyed the firstborn would not touch them.
notes: Grk “the pouring out of the blood.”sn The sprinkling of the blood refers here to the application of the blood to the doorways of the Israelite houses (cf. Exod 12:7, 13).

verses.zh: 他们因着信，过红海如行干地；埃及人试着要过去，就被吞灭了。
verses.en: By faith they crossed the Red Sea as if on dry ground, but when the Egyptians tried it, they were swallowed up.

verses.zh: 以色列人因着信，围绕耶利哥城七日，城墙就倒塌了。
verses.en: By faith the walls of Jericho[NOTE:1] fell after the people marched around them[NOTE:2] for seven days.
notes: For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.
Grk “after they had been encircled.”

verses.zh: 妓女喇合因着信，曾和和平平地接待探子，就不与那些不顺从的人一同灭亡。
verses.en: By faith Rahab the prostitute escaped the destruction of[NOTE:1] the disobedient because she welcomed the spies in peace.
notes: Grk “did not perish together with.”

verses.zh: 我又何必再说呢？若要一一细说，基甸、巴拉、参孙、耶弗他、大卫、撒母耳，和众先知的事，时候就不够了。
verses.en: And what more shall I say? For time will fail me if I tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, of David and Samuel and the prophets.

verses.zh: 他们因着信，制伏了敌国，行了公义，得了应许，堵了狮子的口，
verses.en: Through faith they conquered kingdoms, administered justice,[NOTE:1] gained what was promised,[NOTE:2] shut the mouths of lions,
notes: This probably refers to the righteous rule of David and others. But it could be more general and mean “did what was righteous.”

Grk “obtained promises,” referring to the things God promised, not to the pledges themselves. sn Gained what was promised. They saw some of God’s promises fulfilled, even though the central promise remained unfulfilled until Christ came (cf. vv. 39-40).

verses.zh: 灭了烈火的猛势，脱了刀剑的锋刃；软弱变为刚强，争战显出勇敢，打退外邦的全军。
verses.en: quenched raging fire,[NOTE:1] escaped the edge of the sword, gained strength in weakness,[NOTE:2] became mighty in battle, put foreign armies to flight,
notes: Grk “quenched the power of fire.”
Or “recovered from sickness.”

verses.zh: 有妇人得自己的死人复活。又有人忍受严刑，不肯苟且得释放（原文是赎），为要得着更美的复活。
verses.en: and women received back their dead raised to life.[NOTE:1] But others were tortured, not accepting release, to obtain resurrection to a better life.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “received back their dead from resurrection.”
Grk “to obtain a better resurrection.”

verses.zh: 又有人忍受戏弄、鞭打、捆锁、监禁、各等的磨炼，
verses.en: And others experienced mocking and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment.

verses.zh: 被石头打死，被锯锯死，受试探，被刀杀，披着绵羊、山羊的皮各处奔跑，受穷乏、患难、苦害，
verses.en: They were stoned, sawed apart,[NOTE:1] murdered with the sword; they went about in sheepskins and goatskins; they were destitute, afflicted, ill-treated
notes: The reading ἐπρίσθησαν (epristhēsan, “they were sawed apart”) is found in some significant witnesses (P46 [D* twice reads ἐπίρσθησαν, “they were burned”?] syp sa Orpt Eus). Other mss have ἐπειράσθησαν (epeirasthēsan, “they were tempted”), either before “sawed apart” ([א] L P [048] 33 81 326 1505 syh), after “sawed apart” (P13vid A D1 Ψ 1739 1881 M lat bo Orpt), or altogether in place of “sawed apart” (0150 vgmss Cl). Since the two words ἐπρίσθησαν and ἐπειράσθησαν are so much alike in sight and sound, and since the position of “they were tempted” varies in the mss, it seems best to say that ἐπειράσθησαν is an accidental transcriptional error of ἐπρίσθησαν or an intentional change to a more common word (the root of ἐπρίσθησαν [πρίζω, prizō] occurs only here in the NT, while the root of ἐπειράσθησαν [πειράζω, peirazō] occurs 38 times). The best reading here seems to be “sawed apart” without any addition before or after. (See TCGNT 603-4, for a discussion of emendations that scholars have proposed for this difficult problem.)

verses.zh: 在旷野、山岭、山洞、地穴，飘流无定，本是世界不配有的人。
verses.en: (the world was not worthy of them); they wandered in deserts and mountains and caves and openings in the earth.

verses.zh: 这些人都是因信得了美好的证据，却仍未得着所应许的；
verses.en: And these all were commended[NOTE:1] for their faith, yet they did not receive what was promised.[NOTE:2]
notes: The expression these all were commended forms an inclusio with Heb 11:2: The chapter begins and ends with references to commendation for faith.
Grk “the promise,” referring to the thing God promised, not to the pledge itself.

verses.zh: 因为　神给我们预备了更美的事，叫他们若不与我们同得，就不能完全。
verses.en: For God had provided something better for us, so that they would be made perfect together with us.[NOTE:1]
notes: The Greek phrasing emphasizes this point by negating the opposite: “so that they would not be made perfect without us.”
